stem.text: Let \( g(x) = \int_{x}^{3 x} \frac{1}{t^{2} + 1} \, dt \). Find the exact value of \( g'\left(1\right) \).

worked_solution.text: Split the integral at any constant k in the domain of the integrand: \( g(x) = \int_{k}^{3 x} \frac{1}{t^{2} + 1} \, dt - \int_{k}^{x} \frac{1}{t^{2} + 1} \, dt \), and apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to each piece.
With the chain rule, \( g'(x) = f\left(3 x\right) \cdot 3 - f\left(x\right) \cdot 1 \).
At \( x = 1 \): the limits are \( 3 \) and \( 1 \), with derivatives \( 3 \) and \( 1 \), and \( f\left(3\right) = \frac{1}{10} \), \( f\left(1\right) = \frac{1}{2} \).
